text_blocks.snippet: While some symptoms overlap, COVID-19 and the common cold have distinct differences. COVID-19 is caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, while the common cold is caused by various other viruses. COVID-19 symptoms typically appear 2-14 days after exposure, while cold symptoms usually appear 1-3 days after exposure. COVID-19 can also have more severe symptoms and complications than a cold, including loss of taste or smell and more prolonged illness.
